# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_VALIDATE_ADDRESS::response_t,
#         src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:2592-2607. See
#         validate_address-standard.json for the request flags and the _request_address dispatch rule.
# THIS IS ALSO THE FALLBACK. fmonero-mock dispatches validate_address on the request's `address`,
#         matching it against each fixture's _request_address; WHEN NOTHING MATCHES IT SERVES THIS
#         FILE (DESIGN.md §8 Phase 0). So an address no fixture knows is reported invalid, which is
#         the right default for a mock that cannot verify a checksum.
# AN INVALID ANSWER IS NOT AN ERROR. on_validate_address returns HTTP 200 with valid: false and no
#         JSON-RPC error object; -2 WRONG_ADDRESS "Invalid address"
#         (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:703-705) is what the SEND path gets from `transfer`, not
#         what `validate_address` gets. error-wrong-address.json is that other shape.
# nettype IS THE EMPTY STRING, NOT null AND NOT "unknown", when the address does not parse on any
#         network: on_validate_address only assigns it inside the success branch, and
#         struct_init value-initialises a std::string to "".
# THE ADDRESS is upstream's own bad vector -- tests/functional_tests/validate_address.py:58, where it
#         heads the bad_addresses list and upstream asserts `not res.valid` with any_net_type BOTH
#         true and false (:59-63). It is validate_address.py:68's valid mainnet address with its LAST
#         CHARACTER changed from 'm' to '9': 95 characters, every character in Monero's base58
#         alphabet, decodes to 69 bytes with prefix varint 18 -- STRUCTURALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE from
#         a valid mainnet standard address. Only the 4-byte Keccak checksum is wrong.
# THAT IS EXACTLY WHY §2a.6 VALIDATES TWICE. address::parse (§1b.8, §5b) checks length, base58
#         decodability and the prefix varint -- it does NOT check the checksum, because that needs
#         Keccak-256 and DESIGN.md §3.1 deliberately takes no tiny-keccak dependency. So THIS STRING
#         PASSES address::parse and is caught only by validate_address on the open wallet, which is
#         the authority before any send. A test that asserts "fmonero rejects a bad address" without
#         the wallet daemon up is asserting the structural half only, and this fixture is the one
#         that shows the difference.
